subject: MAP recalibration: authorization for escrow and compressed acceptance windows
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Andrea Liu <andrea@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP recalibration: authorization for escrow and compressed acceptance windows

Andrea —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation, Helix's internal go-live has been pushed three weeks which compresses the evaluation/acceptance runway in the MAP. To keep the project on-track without expanding engineering commitments we need a short MAP recalibration and an escrow authorization so we can limit exposure if the acceptance window narrows.

Proposal (high level):
- New milestone dates attached in MAP_v2 (see attachment).
- Compress acceptance window from 10 business days -> 4 business days for the core eval gate.
- Establish an escrow equal to 10% of the first committed invoice to cover remediation window extension / engineering surge if acceptance extends beyond the compressed window. Escrow releases after acceptance or moves to credit if acceptance fails.

Ask: please confirm in principle (Andrea) so we can route a one-page addendum for signature (DocuSign) and loop your procurement contact. If you want different escrow sizing we can surface options — the 10% is intended to be conservative and avoid a procurement-level credit hold.

Attachments: MAP_v2_HLX_20270909.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

If possible, can procurement confirm they can review the addendum by EOB 9/12? That would keep us aligned for a 9/20 go-live cadence.

Best,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124
Redwood Inference
From: Andrea Liu <andrea@helixhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@procureco.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP recalibration: authorization for escrow and compressed acceptance windows

Grace —

Appreciate the clear proposal. We are aligned with the general approach but procurement needs to see a formal addendum before committing to escrow percentages. Two quick items from our side:
1) procurement will review on 9/12 as requested; they asked for clear release conditions for the escrow and whether escrow can be applied to credits rather than cash hold.
2) our legal team flagged that SLA language around data residency needs to remain unchanged in any addendum. Can you confirm the addendum will be scoped narrowly to acceptance windows & escrow mechanics only?

I attached a PO stub that shows our billing cadence — should help Finance/Legal size the escrow.

Once you send the one-page addendum via DocuSign we will route it internally. We should be able to return a signed confirmation or redline by 9/13.

Thanks,
Andrea

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: MAP recalibration — risk log update and contingency suggestions

Grace / Ben —

I updated the risk log after the Helix call and pulled the probabilities on acceptance failure up one notch. Key entries:
- Risk 112: Compressed acceptance -> missed edge-case tests (probability medium-high). Mitigation: reduce acceptance window to 4 days but require a defined smoke-test checklist that Helix signs off on immediately after deployment.
- Risk 117: Procurement delays on escrow mechanics. Mitigation: offer two escrow options (10% cash hold OR 15% credit note) so procurement can pick the least disruptive.

I attached risk_log_update.xlsx with the changes and a suggested escalation ladder. Operational asks:
1) If Grace sends the one-page addendum, include the smoke-test checklist as an appendix.
2) We should hold a fast-track legal review (2 business days) — can we get Ben to authorize the spend / escrow on the sales side so Finance can do a temporary credit block if they choose credit note instead of cash?

If we greenlight a 10% cash escrow the expected operational impact is minimal; anything above that will require an Exec authorization due to finance exposure.

-Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Quick note before I forward Helix's reply: can you approve the 10% escrow option so I can push the DocuSign addendum to them? Jonas has updated the risk log (attached) and recommends the 10% cash hold or a 15% credit option. Procurement prefers credit notes but that increases reconciliation work for Finance.

If you can give the green light today I will:
- Issue the one-page addendum scoped only to acceptance windows & escrow mechanics (no SLA changes).
- Attach the smoke-test checklist as an appendix.
- Send via DocuSign to Andrea and procurement.
